skill.name: polars
skill.description: Use Polars for high-performance DataFrame work on in-memory datasets. This skill explains expressions, lazy evaluation, I/O, transformations, pandas migration, and performance patterns for 1-100 GB data.
skill.summary: Build faster DataFrame pipelines with Polars expressions, lazy execution, and migration guidance.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder credential snippets, license metadata, and Polars API names. No active code execution, secret access, network exfiltration, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection attempt was found. One low-severity semantic issue remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote an external hosted service for complex workflows.

remediation.issue: External service promotion in skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive promotion or require explicit user consent before suggesting any hosted third-party workflow for user data.

remediation.issue: Credential examples use inline environment assignments
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that credentials are placeholders and recommend secure credential storage or runtime configuration outside copied source code.

static_findings.snippet: For additional best practices and patterns, load `references/best_practices.md`.
- `core_concepts.md` - Detailed explanations of expressions, lazy evaluation, and type system
- `operations.md` - Comprehensive guide to all common operations with examples
- `pandas_migration.md` - Complete migration guide from pandas to Polars
- `io_guide.md` - Data I/O operations for all supported formats
- `transformations.md` - Joins, concatenation, pivots, and reshaping operations

content.value_statement: Large pandas workflows can become slow and hard to optimize. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design Polars pipelines with lazy execution, expressions, and practical migration guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains Polars expressions for select, filter, with_columns, and group_by workflows.
Shows when to use eager DataFrames and lazy LazyFrames for better performance.
Guides CSV, Parquet, JSON, database, cloud storage, and BigQuery I/O patterns.
Maps common pandas operations to equivalent Polars syntax and concepts.
Provides optimization guidance for streaming, projections, data types, joins, and UDF avoidance.
Documents transformations such as joins, concatenation, pivoting, unpivoting, lists, and structs.
limitations: It does not run Polars code unless the host agent has an execution environment.
It is best for datasets that fit in memory, roughly 1-100 GB.
Cloud and database examples require user-managed credentials and connectors.
Version-specific APIs should be checked against the installed Polars release.

use_cases.title: Migrate Slow Pandas Workflows
use_cases.description: Convert common pandas transforms into Polars expressions and lazy pipelines.
use_cases.target_user: Data analysts moving performance-sensitive notebooks or scripts to Polars.

use_cases.title: Design Efficient ETL Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan file ingestion, filtering, aggregation, joins, and output formats for repeatable data processing.
use_cases.target_user: Data engineers building local or cloud-backed batch workflows.

use_cases.title: Tune Analytical Queries
use_cases.description: Use projection pushdown, predicate pushdown, streaming, and native expressions to reduce runtime.
use_cases.target_user: Analytics engineers optimizing medium and large in-memory datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic DataFrame Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first Polars workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a simple Polars workflow that loads a CSV, selects useful columns, filters rows, and writes a clean output file.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Pandas Steps to Polars
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my pandas workflow and explain how to rewrite it in Polars. Focus on expressions, grouping, joins, and differences from pandas indexing.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Lazy Query Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance tuning for larger data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me redesign this Polars pipeline for lazy execution. Look for projection pushdown, predicate pushdown, streaming, and places to avoid Python functions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cloud Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced I/O design across storage and databases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Polars ETL plan for reading partitioned cloud files, joining reference data, aggregating results, and writing Parquet outputs securely.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to speed up a pandas CSV cleanup job.
output_examples.output: The response recommends lazy CSV scanning, early column selection, native expressions, and Parquet output for repeated analysis.

output_examples.input: A data engineer asks how to join and aggregate several medium-size files.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a Polars pipeline with typed inputs, lazy joins, grouped aggregations, and validation checks before writing results.

output_examples.input: An analyst asks why a Polars workflow became slow after adding custom functions.
output_examples.output: The response identifies Python function calls as a likely bottleneck and suggests native expression alternatives where possible.

best_practices: Use lazy scanning for large files so Polars can optimize filters and selected columns.
Prefer native expressions over Python functions to preserve parallel execution.
Choose Parquet and appropriate data types for repeated analysis and efficient storage.
anti_patterns: Do not translate pandas code line by line without considering Polars expressions.
Do not use Python UDFs for operations that native Polars expressions can perform.
Do not load every column eagerly when the query only needs a subset.

faq.question: When should I use Polars instead of pandas?
faq.answer: Use Polars when pandas workflows are too slow and the dataset still fits in memory.

faq.question: Does this skill execute my data pipeline?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance unless the host agent also has a working execution environment.

faq.question: Can it help migrate pandas code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains equivalent Polars patterns and important conceptual differences from pandas.

faq.question: Does it cover cloud storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents S3, Azure, GCS, and BigQuery patterns, but credentials remain your responsibility.

faq.question: Is Polars suitable for larger-than-memory data?
faq.answer: Polars has streaming support, but larger-than-memory workloads may need tools such as Dask or Vaex.

faq.question: What performance topics are included?
faq.answer: It covers lazy execution, predicate pushdown, projection pushdown, streaming, data types, joins, and UDF avoidance.
